A physics-informed network combines observation loss with differential-equation residuals and boundary/initial-condition losses, for example $L=L_{data}+\lambda_r\|\partial_tu-\nu\partial_{xx}u\|^2+\lambda_bL_{boundary}$. Automatic differentiation supplies the derivatives at collocation points. [1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021999118307125)

Soft penalties encourage constraints but do not guarantee them between sampled points. Hard parameterizations can enforce specific boundaries, such as $u(x)=g(x)+x(1-x)f_\theta(x)$ when $g$ has the required endpoint values on [0,1]. Softplus enforces positivity of a scalar, not monotonicity or convexity of an arbitrary network. Those need constrained weights/architectures or integral parameterizations. Scale residual terms carefully and validate against independent numerical solutions, boundary checks, and conservation errors over the full domain.
